faqs.a: Divide your gross pay by your total hours worked: total pay / (regular hours + overtime hours). Because overtime hours are paid at 1.5x, the effective hourly rate always lands above your base rate. For example, $950 for 45 hours gives an effective rate of $21.11 per hour.
faqs.q: What is my effective hourly rate with overtime?

faqs.a: No. The calculator gives gross overtime pay before any deductions. Income tax, Social Security or equivalent contributions, and other withholdings still come out of the total. Your net pay will be lower than the result shown.

Double-time means 2x your hourly rate, usually for working a seventh consecutive day, very long shifts, or public holidays in some contracts. If your contract pays double-time for certain hours, calculate those hours at 2x and add them to the total separately.

Under the US Fair Labor Standards Act, non-exempt employees must receive at least 1.5x their regular rate for hours worked beyond 40 in a work week. Salaried exempt workers are generally not entitled to overtime. Rules vary by country and state, so check your local labour law.
faqs.q: Who is legally entitled to time-and-a-half?

faqs.a: Most employers set the threshold at 40 hours per week. Some places use daily overtime (8+ hours per day) or count holiday hours differently. This calculator lets you set your own regular-hours threshold, so you can match whatever your employer uses.

Yes for many salaried non-exempt workers in the US: the FLSA looks at actual hours worked, not how you are paid. Your regular rate is salary / hours worked, and overtime is 1.5x that rate. Check with your HR department if you are unsure about your classification.

time-and-a-half-calculator.formula:
Overtime rate = hourly rate x 1.5.
Regular pay = hourly rate x regular hours.
Overtime pay = overtime rate x overtime hours.
Total pay = regular pay + overtime pay.
Example: $20 x 1.5 = $30/hour overtime.
howTo: Enter your normal hourly pay rate.
Enter your regular hours (usually 40 per week).
Enter how many extra overtime hours you worked.
Your overtime rate, overtime pay, and total pay appear instantly.
Compare the result with your payslip to make sure every overtime hour was paid.
keyFacts: Time-and-a-half = 1.5 times your normal hourly rate for overtime hours.
Under US federal law, non-exempt employees earn time-and-a-half for hours beyond 40 per week.
The overtime premium is the extra 0.5x on top of your normal rate, so overtime pay adds up faster than people expect.
Some contracts also pay double-time (2x) for holidays or seventh consecutive days.
Salaried workers classified as non-exempt are also entitled to overtime in many cases.
Keep your own record of overtime hours - payslip mistakes are more common than you think.

time-and-a-half-calculator.quickAnswer: Time-and-a-half means your overtime rate is 1.5 times your normal hourly rate. At $20/hour with 5 overtime hours: regular pay is $800, overtime pay is 5 x $30 = $150, total $950. time-and-a-half-calculator.tagline: Work out overtime pay at 1.5x your hourly rate in seconds.
time-and-a-half-calculator.workedExample:
Hourly rate $20, 40 regular hours, 5 overtime hours:
1. Overtime rate = 20 x 1.5 = $30/hour.
2. Regular pay = 20 x 40 = $800.
3. Overtime pay = 30 x 5 = $150.
4. Total pay = 800 + 150 = $950 (gross, before tax).
Effective hourly rate = 950 / 45 = $21.11/hour.
